social.text: Hollywood doesn't actually shoot at 24 FPS. It shoots at 23.976 FPS. 🎥 When color TV launched, NTSC broadcasters had to slow their signal from 30 to 29.97 FPS to stop the color signal from interfering with audio. Film, shot at a true 24 FPS, got the same 0.1% slowdown to stay in sync with NTSC's pulldown process — landing at 23.976 FPS. A 1950s broadcast fix is still shaping how movies are made today. # Filmmaking # Cinematography # FrameRateFacts # NTSC # PostProduction
